sermon.title: Ask of Me 07/23/2017
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Continuing what God said to Jesus, Pastor David G. Kincer teaches Psalm 2: the nations rage against the Lord’s anointed, but God has set his King on Zion and told his Son, “ask of me, and I will give you the nations.” In John 17 Jesus asked not that we be taken out of the world but that we be one, so the world may believe—and Revelation shows a multitude from every nation.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Points to check: New Testament “about 80%” Old Testament verses; Hitler’s “positive Christianity”; survey figures (67% of Christians believe in evolution, 70% of abortions by Christian women, 54% approve same-sex marriage in 2014, 50% approve alcohol/marijuana, 39% literal Bible); alcohol “almost a hundred thousand a year”; Brazil’s 42 uncontacted tribes; Pew-style Africa/Asia-Pacific/Latin America percentages; China “over 200 million Christians”; 2% of Jews Christian; Darby/Miller and 1844. Sensitive content kept as spoken: governments wanting to silence the church; incest “rampant”; a son who tried to take over the church; “thousands … of so-called pastors” not called; Africans coming into the light while Americans go back to “tattoos, bones in our nose”; Catholics “promote drinking”; ex-Muslims: “Allah doesn’t do miracles”; “dumbed down American believers”; denominations ordaining homosexual ministers; prophecy teachers “millionaires from telling you fantasies.”
